result.rationale: The Healthy band is correct on the evidence: all five open invoices sit at 0 days past due and there is no adverse news or parent linkage, so both formula components are genuine zeros rather than gaps in coverage. However, a score of exactly 0.0 overstates the comfort available here. The payment agent's own review (INV001494) flags that the sole settled invoice on record was paid 28 days late against a 90-day term, that trend is explicitly "insufficient_history", and that open exposure of EUR 695.5k runs to roughly 79% of the single EUR 880k limit — none of which a current-DPD-only payment score can capture. I recommend the underwriter treat this as a thin-file Healthy with limited headroom rather than a clean risk.

concerns.issue: The payment score reads 0.0 off current DPD only and therefore ignores the single settled invoice on record (INV001489, EUR 195k), which was paid 28 days late against a 90-day term. With trend recorded as 'insufficient_history', the 0 DPD reading reflects invoices not yet due rather than a demonstrated record of paying on time.

Concentration and headroom are outside the formula entirely. Open exposure of EUR 695.5k across five invoices equals about 79% of the sole insurer's EUR 880k credit limit, leaving little buffer if the 28-day lateness seen on the one settled invoice recurs across the open book.
The credit limit was last reviewed in Jan 2025, over a year before this review dated 2026-09-15, so the EUR 880k limit against which utilisation is measured may not reflect current exposure levels.

Staleness of the underlying payment snapshot: the 0 DPD observation is dated 2026-06-24 while the payment review is dated 2026-09-15, a gap of nearly three months. On the 90-day terms cited in INV001494, invoices open at the June snapshot could have reached or passed their due date without being reflected in the score.
